docs.text: Field Description Default namespaces.keycloak Namespace for Keycloak pods keycloak namespaces.tasks Namespace where analytics task pods run tasks namespaces.controller Namespace for the Task Controller pods fn-controller

docs.title: Token
docs.text: Field Description Default token.life Auth token lifetime in seconds 2592000 (30 days)

docs.title: Networking and access control
docs.text: Field Description Default integrations.domains List of third-party origins permitted by CORS/CSP policy. Only relevant when a web UI accesses the FN - does not affect direct API usage. [self] whitelist.enabled Enable IP CIDR allowlist - whitelist.ips List of allowed IP CIDRs - blacklist.enabled Enable IP CIDR blocklist - blacklist.ips List of blocked IP CIDRs -

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: Field Description Default tls.secretName Kubernetes secret name containing the TLS certificate tls

docs.title: Traefik (ingress)
docs.text: Field Description Default traefik.enabled Enable the Traefik reverse proxy subchart. Requires Gateway API and Traefik CRDs to be pre-installed. See Prerequisites. false traefik.gateway.enabled Enable the Traefik Gateway resource false traefik.gateway.name Name of the Gateway resource traefik-fn-gateway traefik.gatewayClass.name Name of the GatewayClass traefik-fn-gateway-class traefik.api.dashboard Enable the Traefik dashboard false traefik.service.spec.externalIPs List of external IPs to assign to the Traefik service - traefik.service.spec.externalTrafficPolicy AKS deployments only. Options: Local, Cluster Local

docs.text: Field Description Default cert-manager.enabled Enable the cert-manager subchart false cert-manager.namespace Namespace for cert-manager resources fn-certmanager cert-manager.installCRDs Install cert-manager CRDs automatically true certs.rotationPolicy Certificate rotation policy Never certs.azure.secretName Secret name for the Azure SP used in SSL renewal - certs.azure.configmap ConfigMap name for Azure SP SSL renewal configuration - certs.aws Secret name containing AWS Route 53 credentials for SSL renewal -

docs.title: Task Controller subchart
docs.text:
These fields are only used when outboundMode: true. See Task Controller: Deploy for full details.

Field Description Default fn-task-controller.controller.tag Task Controller image tag Chart appVersion fn-task-controller.controller.skipUserAuth Skip GitHub identity verification. When true, tasks run as the controller's system user rather than verifying the submitting GitHub user. true fn-task-controller.controller.vol_path Internal volume mount path for the controller - fn-task-controller.storage.* Same structure as main storage.*, including mountOptions - fn-task-controller.idp.github.secret_name Kubernetes secret name containing the GitHub App credentials - fn-task-controller.idp.github.secret_key Key in the secret for the GitHub App client secret - fn-task-controller.idp.github.clientid_key Key in the secret for the GitHub App client ID - fn-task-controller.idp.github.orgAndRepo GitHub org/repo that researchers submit tasks from - fn-task-controller.delivery.github.repository GitHub org/repo where results are pushed - fn-task-controller.delivery.other.url Alternative delivery destination hostname (no http:// prefix) - fn-task-controller.delivery.other.auth_type Auth type for other delivery. Options: Bearer, AzCopy, Basic -

docs.text:
These fields exist for local development and should not be used in production.

Field Description Default local_development Disables SSL validation - for local development only false create_db_deployment Deploy an in-cluster PostgreSQL instance - unstable, not for production false

docs.title: Installing ArgoCD
docs.text: We recommend using ArgoCD to manage deployments of the Federated Node, this article explains how to install it for use with the FN. Additionally, where the FN is deployed in outbound mode ArgoCD is used to detect new tasks.

docs.title: ArgoCD files
docs.text:
Navigate to the ArgoCD folder and run the installation script

This will: - add the argoCD helm repository locally (just as listing) - install the latest argo version with some of our custom configuration - add the two github repository as available sources when adding a new application.

Once the installation is completed, argo can be accessed by "bridging" a connection: 

kubectl port-forward service/argocd-server -n argocd 8000:443
This will allow you to access the UI at localhost:8000

You will need a set of credentials, which are stored in a kubernetes secret 

kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret -o json | jq -r '.data | .[] |= @base64d'
Note that this should be used as a temporary password, and should be changed after the first login. More details in the ArgoCD official docs

docs.title: Add an application
docs.text:
In terms of Argo ecosystem, an application can be interchangeably used as deployment. This can be done in two ways: - via the CLI using a .yaml file - via the UI

Most cases within the Federated Node we will be dealing with an helm chart as an application.

docs.title: Via the UI
docs.text: Once logged in, you will be greeted with this screen:

docs.title: Installing ArgoCD
docs.text:
By clicking on Create application, the following will appear: - Fill up the form, by setting the Application Name to something it can be recognized. - Set the project name to default, it should be a dropdown menu. - Set the sync policy to Manual if you want to have control when to perform an update, or Automatic if you want to install them as they come

This section is mostly autocomplete/dropdown choices - Set the repository name to the PHEMS_federated_node option - Revision in case of a git repository refers to the branch you want to monitor and pull changes from, let's say this is going to be main. Deleting the existing field value HEAD will prompt with all the available branches - Path will be updated automatically after the Revision. Argo will autodetect suitable paths, at this time should be k8s/federated-node

Here we should tell where to install the application - Cluster URL should be the only available choice https://kubernetes.default.svc. - Namespace should be the base where the application will be installed to. Set it to default (no autocomplete here) if no preference.

Here we set the specific helm chart related configuration

in the red-highlighted box the contents of the values.yaml file should be pasted. These values should be set if they differ from the default ones. For more info, have a look at the deployment instructions

docs.title: Via the CLI
docs.text:
It would be preferable for the CLI to be installed (The CLI should be installed as part of the argo installation script). This can be verified by running: 

argocd version
if succesful something like this should be returned 
argocd: v2.13.1+af54ef8
  BuildDate: 2024-11-20T16:54:29Z
  GitCommit: af54ef8db5adfa77a08d4d05b1318a2198084c22
  GitTreeState: clean
  GoVersion: go1.22.9
  Compiler: gc
  Platform: linux/amd64

To add an application you would need a yaml file representing the app, an example is provided here

Once this file exists with the appropriate contents 

argocd app create <application-name> --file <path-to-yaml-file>
Or 
kubectl apply -f fn_application.yaml
More details here

docs.title: Outbound Connection Only Mode
docs.text:
If your cluster cannot accept inbound connections from researchers, or if you are joining a federated network that requires a standardised task submission workflow, the Federated Node can run in outbound mode using the Federated Node Task Controller (FNTC).

In outbound mode, researchers do not call the FN API directly. Instead, they submit tasks via a GitHub repository. The Task Controller monitors that repository and - from inside your cluster - calls the FN API internally when a task is submitted, then pushes results back to GitHub when the task completes.

docs.title: Enabling outbound mode
docs.text:
The Task Controller is bundled as a subchart in the FN Helm chart. Enable it by adding to your values.yaml:

outboundMode: true

Additional configuration for the Task Controller goes under fn-task-controller. A minimal example:

outboundMode: true

fn-task-controller:
  storage:
    local:
      path: /data/controller

  idp:
    github:
      secret_name: myorg-my-task-repo
      secret_key: GH_SECRET
      clientid_key: GH_CLIENT_ID
      orgAndRepo: MyOrg/My-Task-Repo

  delivery:
    github:
      repository: MyOrg/My-Task-Repo

See the Helm Values Reference for all fn-task-controller configuration options.

docs.title: Full setup guide
docs.text:
Complete setup documentation is in the Task Controller wiki:

  • Overview - how the Task Controller works and when to use it
  • GitHub Setup - create the GitHub App, repository, and Actions pipeline
  • Deploy - configure and deploy the controller
  • Running Tasks - how researchers submit tasks and retrieve results

docs.title: Post-Deploy Testing
docs.text: Use this guide to verify your Federated Node is healthy and fully functional before handing it over to users or setting up the Task Controller.

docs.title: 1. Check pod status
docs.text:
kubectl get pods -n federated-node
kubectl get pods -n keycloak
kubectl get pods -n tasks

All pods should reach Running status. Keycloak can take 1–2 minutes on first boot.

If anything is stuck, check its logs:

kubectl logs -n federated-node deployment/backend
kubectl logs -n keycloak statefulset/keycloak

docs.title: 2. Set your hostname
docs.text:
Set the FN hostname in an environment variable. All examples in this guide use $FN_HOST.

If accessing via a public hostname: 

export FN_HOST=https://fn.your-institution.example.com

If port-forwarding to the backend directly (no Traefik): 

kubectl port-forward -n federated-node service/backend 5000
export FN_HOST=http://localhost:5000

If port-forwarding through Traefik: 

# Note: the service name includes your helm release name (federatednode)
kubectl port-forward -n federated-node service/federatednode-traefik 443:443
export FN_HOST=https://localhost

docs.title: 3. Health check
docs.text:
curl "$FN_HOST/health_check"

Expected response:

{
    "status": "ok",
    "keycloak": true
}

If keycloak is false, Keycloak hasn't finished starting. Wait 30 seconds and retry. If it stays false, check Keycloak logs.

docs.title: 4. Login
docs.text:
If you configured firstUserSecret, use that email and password. Otherwise retrieve the auto-generated password:

PASSWORD=$(kubectl get secret -n federated-node kc-secrets -o json \
  | jq -r '.data.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD' | base64 -d)

Log in and save the token:

TOKEN=$(curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/login" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
    --data-urlencode "username=admin@your-institution.example.com" \
    --data-urlencode "password=$PASSWORD" | jq -r '.token')

echo $TOKEN

You should see a JWT string. If you get an error, confirm Keycloak is healthy (step 3) and that the username/password are correct.

All subsequent API calls pass this token as Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN. Tokens are valid for 30 days by default.

docs.title: 5. Create a test dataset
docs.text:
A dataset registration tells the FN where your research database lives. The FN stores the connection details - it never copies or centralises the data.

curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/datasets/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "name": "test-dataset",
        "host": "your-database-host.example.com",
        "port": 5432,
        "username": "db-user",
        "password": "db-password",
        "type": "postgres",
        "schema": "public"
    }' | jq .

The type field sets the database engine. Options: postgres, mssql, mysql, oracle, mariadb, and from v1.21.0 duckdb and sqlite. Defaults to postgres if omitted. See Datasets for examples of each.

Expected response:

{ "dataset_id": 1, "url": "https://<host>/datasets/test-dataset" }

Confirm it was saved:

curl --silent "$FN_HOST/datasets/" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .

docs.title: 6. Register a container registry and allowlist an image
docs.text:
The FN controls which images can run against your data via a registry allowlist. First register the registry:

curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/registries/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "url": "ghcr.io/your-org",
        "username": "your-github-username",
        "password": "your-github-PAT"
    }' | jq .

Then allowlist a specific image (only needed if federatedNode.enable_image_whitelist: true):

curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/containers" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "name": "test-analysis",
        "registry": "ghcr.io/your-org",
        "tag": "1.0"
    }' | jq .

Note: Image whitelisting is off by default (federatedNode.enable_image_whitelist: false). When off, any image from a registered registry can run. Enable it for tighter control in production.

docs.title: 7. Submit a test task
docs.text:
TASK=$(curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/tasks/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "name": "smoke-test",
        "executors": [
            {
                "image": "ghcr.io/your-org/test-analysis:1.0"
            }
        ],
        "tags": {
            "dataset_id": 1
        },
        "description": "Post-deploy smoke test"
    }')

echo $TASK | jq .
TASK_ID=$(echo $TASK | jq -r '.task_id')

Watch the task pod appear in the tasks namespace:

kubectl get pods -n tasks

Check task status:

curl --silent "$FN_HOST/tasks/$TASK_ID" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.status'

docs.title: 8. Retrieve results
docs.text:
Once status is COMPLETE:

curl --silent "$FN_HOST/tasks/$TASK_ID/results" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --output results.tar.gz

tar -tzf results.tar.gz

If taskReview is enabled in your values, an admin must approve results before they can be retrieved. See Task Review.

Note: The cleanup CronJob removes task results and related Kubernetes resources daily at noon, after cleanupTime days (default: 3). Retrieve results before then.

docs.title: All checks passed?
docs.text:
Your Federated Node is working. Next steps:

  • Set up users and dataset permissions → User Roles and Using the API
  • Enable the results review workflow → Task Review
  • Deploy the Task Controller for outbound-only mode → Task Controller Overview
  • Build analytics containers → Analytics Container Development

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before deploying the Federated Node, make sure the following are in place.

docs.title: Required tools
docs.text:
Tool Purpose Install guide kubectl Interact with your Kubernetes cluster docs.kubernetes.io helm (v3+) Deploy the FN chart helm.sh/docs/intro/install jq Parse API responses in shell examples stedolan.github.io/jq

Example values.yaml files for each platform are provided throughout the deploy guides in this documentation.

docs.title: Kubernetes cluster
docs.text:
Any CNCF-conformant Kubernetes cluster works. Tested platforms:

  • Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
  • AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS)
  • Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
  • On-premises (RKE2)

Other CNCF-conformant distributions should work but have not been formally tested.

Minimum recommended node specs: 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM. Analytics task pods spin up alongside the base FN pods, so size your cluster for your expected concurrent workload.

docs.title: PostgreSQL database
docs.text:
The FN needs a PostgreSQL instance for its own internal metadata (users, datasets, task records, audit logs). This is not the database containing your research data.

  • PostgreSQL 12+ works (managed or self-hosted)
  • The FN creates its own schema on first startup via Alembic migrations
  • You need the hostname, port, database name, username, and password ready before deploying

docs.title: Persistent storage
docs.text:
The FN needs a persistent volume to temporarily hold task results between job completion and the researcher retrieving them. Four storage backends are supported:

  • Azure File Share - for AKS deployments
  • AWS EFS - for EKS deployments
  • Google Cloud Storage - For GKE deployments
  • NFS - cloud-agnostic, on-prem friendly
  • Local host path - single-node / development only

See the platform-specific deploy guide for configuration details.

docs.title: Critical: pre-install Gateway API and Traefik CRDs
docs.text:
If you plan to use Traefik as the ingress controller (traefik.enabled: true, recommended for production), you must install two sets of Kubernetes CRDs before running helm install. The chart will fail at install time with a clear error message if these are missing.

# 1. Gateway API CRDs
kubectl apply --server-side -f \
  "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.4.0/standard-install.yaml"

# 2. Traefik CRDs
kubectl apply --server-side -f \
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/traefik/traefik/v3.6/docs/content/reference/dynamic-configuration/kubernetes-crd-definition-v1.yml"

This is a one-time step per cluster. If you are deploying without Traefik (traefik.enabled: false), you can skip it.

docs.title: Notes on secrets
docs.text:
The FN values file supports referencing pre-created Kubernetes secrets rather than embedding credentials as plain text. This is strongly recommended for production.

A few characters cause problems in shell --from-literal commands: " must be escaped as \", and % requires special handling. When in doubt, use the YAML manifest approach and pre-encode values with echo -n "yourvalue" | base64.

If you plan to deploy into a non-default namespace, create it before creating any secrets - secrets created in the wrong namespace won't be visible to the FN pods:

kubectl create namespace <your-namespace>

docs.title: Next step
docs.text:
Follow the deploy guide for your platform - start with Deploy: Core, which covers steps common to all platforms, then add your platform-specific guide alongside it:

  • Deploy: Azure (AKS)
  • Deploy: AWS (EKS)
  • Deploy: GCP (GKE)
  • Deploy: On-Premises

docs.title: Task Review (v1.3.0+)
docs.text:
Task Review is an optional governance feature that holds task results until an administrator has inspected and explicitly approved them. This is useful for institutions that need to verify results don't inadvertently leak sensitive information before they leave the node.

By default this feature is disabled - results are available to the requesting user as soon as the task completes.

docs.title: Enabling Task Review
docs.text:
In values.yaml:

taskReview: true

Or at deploy/upgrade time:

helm upgrade federatednode federated-node/federated-node \
    -f values.yaml \
    --set taskReview=true \
    --namespace federated-node

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
When enabled:

  1. A researcher submits a task (via API or Task Controller) - this is unchanged
  2. The task runs and completes
  3. Results are held - the researcher cannot retrieve them, and if using the Task Controller, automatic delivery is also paused
  4. An administrator reviews the results by calling GET /tasks/<id>/results - this returns the results to the admin only
  5. The administrator either approves or blocks the results

docs.title: Approving results
docs.text:
Once satisfied the results are safe to release:

curl --request POST "$FN_HOST/tasks/<task-id>/results/approve" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

After approval, the researcher can retrieve results via GET /tasks/<id>/results. If using the Task Controller, automatic delivery to the configured destination also proceeds.

docs.title: Blocking results
docs.text:
To prevent results from being released (recorded in the audit log):

curl --request POST "$FN_HOST/tasks/<task-id>/results/block" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Blocking is primarily for audit trail purposes. The FN does not send automatic notifications - if you block results, inform the researcher through your own processes.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Task Review applies regardless of how a task was triggered (direct API call or Task Controller)
  • The cleanupTime setting still applies - results will be cleaned up after that many days even if not approved, so review promptly
  • Results held for review are visible to administrators only via GET /tasks/<id>/results

docs.title: User Roles and Permissions
docs.text: The Federated Node uses Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) managed through Keycloak.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Role Typical use Super Administrator Full access to everything Administrator Full access to everything (same as Super Admin via the FN API) System Service accounts and automation - full task/dataset access, no user management User Researchers - limited by default, permissions granted per-dataset

docs.title: Permissions by role
docs.text: Permission Super Admin Admin System User can_admin_dataset ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ can_exec_task ✅ ✅ ✅ Dataset grant only can_admin_task ✅ ✅ ✅ Dataset grant only can_access_dataset ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ can_transfer_token ✅ ✅ ✅ Dataset grant only can_do_admin ✅ ✅ ❌ ✅ can_send_request ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ can_admin_request ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌

docs.title: Permission descriptions
docs.text: Permission Description can_admin_dataset Create, edit, and delete dataset mappings can_exec_task Submit a task to run against a dataset can_admin_task View task logs and cancel running tasks can_access_dataset View dataset connection metadata (not the underlying data) can_transfer_token Retrieve an access token after dataset access is granted can_do_admin Access audit logs, the service-info endpoint, and create/list FN users can_send_request Submit a data access request for a dataset can_admin_request Manage data access requests (currently inactive)

docs.title: Granting users access to datasets
docs.text:
A User cannot run tasks until an administrator grants them access to a specific dataset via the token_transfer endpoint. After this grant they receive can_exec_task, can_admin_task, and can_transfer_token scoped to that dataset only.

See Using the API for the token_transfer API call.

docs.title: Creating users
docs.text:
curl --location "$FN_HOST/users/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "email": "researcher@institution.com",
        "role": "User"
    }'

If the user doesn't already exist in Keycloak they are created automatically. Administrator accounts must be configured via firstUserSecret at deploy time or directly in Keycloak - they cannot be created through the FN API.

docs.title: Using the API
docs.text:
This guide covers everyday API interactions for administrators and researchers. Full interactive API docs are available at https://aridhia-open-source.github.io/PHEMS_federated_node/

We also provide a Postman collection with some degree of response automation.

You can find it in the repository: https://github.com/Aridhia-Open-Source/federatednode-postman

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: export FN_HOST=https://fn.your-institution.example.com

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
TOKEN=$(curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/login" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
    --data-urlencode "username=your@email.com" \
    --data-urlencode "password=yourpassword" | jq -r '.token')

Tokens are valid for 30 days by default (configurable via token.life). The token survives cluster restarts.

All subsequent calls pass the token as: --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Refresh a token
docs.text:
A token can be refreshed before it expires. Ideally do this every 29 days to avoid downtime.

TOKEN=$(curl --silent --location "$FN_HOST/refresh_token" \
    --request POST \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq -r '.token')

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Datasets are connection mappings to research databases. The FN stores connection details only - data never leaves its source.

See Datasets for per-engine examples (PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle) and for DuckDB/SQLite file datasets.

docs.title: Register a dataset (admin only)
docs.text:
curl --location "$FN_HOST/datasets/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "name": "my-dataset",
        "host": "db.your-institution.example.com",
        "port": 5432,
        "username": "db_user",
        "password": "db_password",
        "type": "postgres",
        "schema": "public",
        "schema_write": "results",
        "repository": "your-org/your-task-repo"
    }'

Field notes:

  • type - database engine. Options: postgres, mssql, mysql, oracle, mariadb, and from v1.21.0 duckdb and sqlite. Defaults to postgres.
  • port - defaults to 5432 whatever the engine, so set it for non-PostgreSQL databases.
  • schema - read schema, passed to analytics containers as CDM_SCHEMA
  • schema_write - write schema, passed to analytics containers as WRITE_SCHEMA
  • repository - link this dataset to a GitHub repository for outbound mode. When a task CRD comes from this repo, it maps automatically to this dataset. Only one dataset can be linked to a given repository.

Response: { "dataset_id": 1, "url": "https://<host>/datasets/my-dataset" }

docs.title: List datasets
docs.text:
curl "$FN_HOST/datasets/" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Update a dataset
docs.text:
curl --request PATCH "$FN_HOST/datasets/1" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "schema": "new_schema",
        "schema_write": "new_results_schema"
    }'

docs.title: Delete a dataset (admin only)
docs.text:
Deletes the dataset mapping, its credentials secret, and any linked catalogues and dictionaries.

curl --request DELETE "$FN_HOST/datasets/1" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Create a user (admin only)
docs.text:
curl --location "$FN_HOST/users/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "email": "researcher@institution.com",
        "role": "User"
    }'

Available roles: Super Administrator, Administrator, User. See User Roles.

If the user doesn't already exist in Keycloak they will be created. Administrator accounts cannot be created via the API - use firstUserSecret at deploy time or Keycloak directly.

docs.title: Grant a user access to a dataset
docs.text:
Users with the User role cannot run tasks until they've been granted access to a specific dataset.

curl --location "$FN_HOST/datasets/token_transfer" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "title": "Research Project X",
        "project_name": "project-x",
        "requested_by": {
            "email": "researcher@institution.com"
        },
        "description": "Access for benchmarking study",
        "proj_start": "2024-10-01",
        "proj_end": "2025-10-01",
        "dataset_id": 1
    }'

docs.title: Container registries
docs.text: The FN controls which images can run against your data. Registries must be explicitly registered, and images can optionally be restricted to an allowlist.

docs.title: Register a registry (admin only)
docs.text:
curl --location "$FN_HOST/registries/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "url": "ghcr.io/your-org",
        "username": "github-username",
        "password": "github-PAT"
    }'

docs.title: Update registry credentials
docs.text:
curl --request PATCH "$FN_HOST/registries/1" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "password": "new-github-PAT"
    }'

docs.title: Delete a registry (admin only)
docs.text:
Removes the registry and all associated container allowlist entries.

curl --request DELETE "$FN_HOST/registries/1" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Allowlist an image (admin only)
docs.text:
Only relevant when federatedNode.enable_image_whitelist: true. When image whitelisting is off (the default), any image from a registered registry is allowed.

curl --location "$FN_HOST/containers" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "name": "my-analysis",
        "registry": "ghcr.io/your-org",
        "tag": "1.0"
    }'

docs.title: Submit a task
docs.text:
curl --location "$FN_HOST/tasks/" \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --data '{
        "name": "my-analysis",
        "executors": [
            {
                "image": "ghcr.io/your-org/my-analysis:1.0",
                "env": {
                    "MY_PARAM": "value"
                }
            }
        ],
        "tags": {
            "dataset_id": 1
        },
        "description": "Running benchmarking analysis"
    }'

Additional optional fields in the task body:

  • executors[].env - key/value pairs passed as environment variables to the analytics container (in addition to the standard DB connection vars)
  • db_query - pre-fetch data from the dataset DB before the container runs (see Analytics Container Development)
  • inputs - input file mappings
  • outputs - output path mappings

docs.title: Check task status
docs.text:
curl "$FN_HOST/tasks/$TASK_ID" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: List all tasks (admin only)
docs.text:
curl "$FN_HOST/tasks/" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Cancel a task (admin only)
docs.text:
curl --request POST "$FN_HOST/tasks/$TASK_ID/cancel" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Retrieve results
docs.text:
Once status is COMPLETE (and approved if task review is enabled):

curl "$FN_HOST/tasks/$TASK_ID/results" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    --output results.tar.gz

docs.title: Audit logs
docs.text:
curl "$FN_HOST/admin/audit" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
